subject: Post-demo: Integration plan & JSON validation strategy

Subject: Post-demo: Integration plan & JSON validation strategy

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the demo today; appreciated the clear overview of DataCraft's ingestion pipeline and the user flows you want to enable with LLM-driven synthesis. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on an integration plan: 

1) What we heard from you
- Real-time enrichment on API intake (low latency, <200ms p95 target)
- Deterministic structured outputs for downstream systems (orders, categorization)
- Embeddings for semantic search + reranking for result prioritization

2) Proposed Redwood approach (high-level)
- SDK-based client to call Redwood hosted endpoints for generation + embedding. Client handles auth (short-lived tokens), batching, and fallback routing to a smaller quantized model for cost/availability.
- Constrained decoding using a JSON-schema + constrained-sampling layer so responses conform to expected fields. Validation + retry logic on the SDK side to handle partial decode failures.

Questions for your engineering team (quick):
- Do you control the client environment (server side only) or do you plan any browser/web-app calls?
- Do you have an existing auth system we should federate with (OIDC, SAML, or custom API key rotation)?
- Expected throughput (rps) for enrichment and re-ranker calls in steady state and peak?

Next steps I propose:
- We draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes a minimal PoC: SDK setup guide, example JSON schema for the primary structured output, and an outline of auth/routing.
- Technical sync with your engineers (30–45 min) to confirm SDK auth flows and embedding storage/refresh cadence.

I've attached a short SDK setup checklist and drafted a sample JSON Schema for the MVP structured output — take a look and we'll iterate.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Dev / Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers below then happy to set the tech sync: 

- Client environment: server-side only for now (we're proxying calls from our API layer). No browser calls in the initial phase.
- Auth: we run OIDC with short-lived access tokens backed by our IdP (Okta). Long-term we'd prefer token exchange / service-to-service flow rather than static API keys.
- Throughput: baseline ~30 rps for enrichment, spikes to ~200 rps during business hours for heavy batches. Embedding pipeline is lower QPS (5–10 rps) but higher throughput in batched offline jobs.

About constrained decoding: we care most about schema adherence for order-reconciliation fields (order_id, total_amount, currency, line_items). If the model returns an invalid payload, we should retry once automatically and escalate if still failing.

I'll loop in our infra lead if that helps confirm IAM details — copying Solutions for scheduling.

—Emily

Emily —

Quick technical reply with the patterns we recommend and what we'll hand off in the PoC: 

1) SDK auth pattern
- We support OIDC token exchange (RFC 8693) / OAuth2 client credentials and short-lived session tokens. For your Okta setup we can recommend a token-exchange flow so you never store long-lived API keys.

2) Routing and availability
- Default routing: region-aware endpoint selection (US primary, fallback to dedicated lower-cost model pool if p95 latency > threshold).
- You can pin a model variant for strict deterministic outputs (we'll recommend a tuned model+quant profile).

3) Structured output reliability (core)
- Constrained decoding: we emit token-level constraints derived from the provided JSON Schema to bias the decoder. Works best when the schema is expressive but not overly permissive for enumerated fields.
- Validation pipeline: SDK performs a local schema validation pass. If validation fails, SDK will request one automatic retry with a different sampling seed and stricter decoding constraints. If still failing, we return a structured error with the last-good partial payload and flags for server-side replay.
- Retry pattern details: primary call -> if invalid -> sdk-local-retry (1) synchronous -> if still invalid -> return 4xx structured validation error with diagnostics. For high-value transactions we recommend a synchronous fanout: call both the constrained generator and a fallback deterministic model; reconcile results server-side and prefer deterministic if schema mismatch occurs.

4) Embeddings + reranker notes
- We'll provide an embeddings batching helper in the SDK and a reranker stub that accepts candidate IDs + embeddings to return a reranked list. We'll recommend using vector DB + periodic refresh jobs for large corpora.

PoC deliverables from Redwood: SDK checklist, sample client code (Python + Node), JSON Schema for order-recon MVP, and a local validation harness. Stephanie will own the SDK sample and the validation harness.

Happy to join the tech sync — suggest Wed 20 May at 10am PT.

-Rishi

Emily — thanks for the answers and for committing to bring your infra lead. To keep momentum, here is a short mutual action plan (MAP) and immediate next steps.

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (MVP)
- PoC window: 3 weeks starting 2026-05-25
- Redwood deliverables (by 2026-05-27):
  * SDK setup checklist (attached) + Python/Node quickstarts (auth+call examples)
  * JSON Schema: datacraft-integration-mvp.jsonschema (attached) covering order_id, total_amount, currency, line_items (min fields)
  * Local validation harness and sample test vectors
- DataCraft deliverables (by 2026-05-27):
  * Okta team contact + test OIDC client credentials for token exchange
  * Representative sample payloads and the DB schema for line_items

TECH SYNC: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:00 PT — confirmed? If timing doesn't work, propose Thu 21 May 9:00 PT.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA FOR PO C
- Structured outputs validate against the JSON Schema for >= 95% of test vectors without manual correction.
- Latency p95 for generation path < 250ms in your staging environment under 50 rps.

Open questions / risks
- If Okta token exchange isn't approved, we should fall back to short-lived API keys for PoC and swap to token-exchange in production.
- Edge cases for line_items (nested arrays with optional metadata) can blow up schema complexity — we'll start with a constrained canonical shape and iterate.

Please reply here to confirm the MAP and attach your Okta contact. I'll send calendar invites and a Drive folder with the PoC artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Dev Patel
